## Load required packages

This document uses the following R packages and environment setup.

```{r packages}
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| fig-height: 3
library("tidyverse"); library("patchwork"); library("ggplot2")
library("scales"); library("glue"); library("tibble");library("tidyquant");
library(tidytuesdayR); tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2022, week = 13)
theme_set(theme_minimal())
theme_update(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## Question 1

### 1. a.

```{r q1-a}
sports <- tuesdata$sports |> 
  tibble()
sports |> glimpse()
```
The dataset contains 132,327 observations and 28 variables. Each observation represents a college athletic team (by school, year, paticipants, and sport).
\newpage

### 1. b.

```{r q1-b}
sports |> ggplot(aes(exp_men)) +
  geom_histogram(boundary = 0, bins = 150, color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_log10(
    labels = c("$1k","$10k","$100k","$1mil","$10mil","$100mil"),
    breaks = 10^(3:8)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), n.breaks = 10) +
  labs(
    title = "School Expenditures by Men",
    x = "Expenditures (Men)",
    y = "Number of Teams"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1000, NA)) +
  theme_minimal()
```
\newpage

### 1. c.

```{r q1-c}
sports |>
  count(classification_name) |>
  nrow()
```
There are 19 observations in classification_name
\newpage

### 1. d.

```{r q1-d}
d1_fbs <- sports |> filter(classification_name == "NCAA Division I-FBS")
d1_fbs |> glimpse()
```
\newpage

### 1. e.

```{r q1-e}
d1_fbs |> 
  count(institution_name) |>
  nrow()
```
There are 130 schools in NCAA FBS-Division I.
\newpage

### 1. f.

```{r q1-f}
d1_fbs |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(exp_men, rev_men, color = "Men"), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(exp_women, rev_women, color = "Women"), na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Expenditures",
    labels = label_dollar(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Revenues",
    labels = label_dollar(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Expenditures and Revenues compared in D1 FBS Schools"
  )
```
From this graphic, we can clearly see that there is significantly higher expenditure and revenue in men's Division 1 FBS schools. It it also clear that there is a positive relationship between expenditures, and revenue.
\newpage

### 1. g.

```{r q1-g}
```
General trend: The scatterplot shows a strong positive relationship between expenditures and revenues among D1 FBS programs and it is clear that schools that spend more tend to earn more.

Local Behavior: Most schools are grouped in the $0.1M – $5M expenditure range. and there is significant overplotting in this region. Once you reach more than $20M in expenditures, and more than $50M in revenues, the plot becomes much more clear. Small schools cluster near the origin, while some larger schools have very high revenue and very high expenditure.

Outliers: You can see that there are only a few schools outside of the $60M expenditures range, and only one school with more than $150M in revenue. Despite this, these points still follow the general trend of high reveneue leading to high expenditure, and there are no outliers in this graphic.

\newpage

### 1. h.

```{r q1-h}
d1_fbs |>
  filter(
    state_cd == "TX",
    sports == "Football"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(rev_men, reorder(institution_name, rev_men))) +
  geom_jitter(height = .1, size = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = label_dollar(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Football Revenues for Texas D1 FBS Schools",
    subtitle = "2015-2019",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)
  )
```
For question 1.h. I used ChatGPT5 to help me change the x and y axis element font size, allowing for more room for the actual graphic when rendering. Also, the $160M was slightly cut off, so I lowered the font size so everything fits better and looks more presentable.
\newpage

### 1. i.

```{r q1-i}
d1_fbs |>
  filter(
    state_cd == "TX", 
    sports == "Football"
  ) |>
  mutate(net_return = rev_men / exp_men - 1) |>
  ggplot(aes(net_return, reorder(institution_name, net_return))) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1),
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Net Return on Football Programs",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)
  )
```
The schools that "make money" on football appear to be The University of Texas, Texas Tech, Texas A&M, Texas Christian University, Baylor, UT at El Paso, and University of North Texas.

For question 1.i. I used ChatGPT5 to help me with two things: First was changing from geom_jitter to geom_col, I explained to ChatGPT that I did not like the appearance of the plot when geom_jitter was applied, to which it recommended using geom_col. Second, I needed help with how to use label_percent and understand what accuracy did. ChatGPT Helped me format the gome_col, and where and how to implement label_percent.
